WELCOME TOWELLINGTON COMMUNITY PRIMARY SCHOOL
We trust that you find your visit to our school website informative and fun, giving an insight into what we are all about! We are a two-form-entry primary school with over 400 pupils on roll, aged 4 to 11 years. We are a popular school with an excellent reputation in the local and wider community.
As you navigate through our website, you will see that we offer a wide range of extra-curricular activities and after-school clubs, catering for a range of ages and interests across the school including a range of sports, dance and music. Children have plentiful opportunities to participate in sporting fixtures and musical provision.
DATES FORYour Diary
We’ve seen our child grow so much since starting here – not just in learning but in confidence too. They’re really thriving and we couldn’t be happier.
It’s brilliant hearing my child talk about what they’re learning. They’re curious and proud of what they’ve achieved. They really see themselves as a learner.
My child is always happy going to school and comes home chatting about their day. It’s clear they feel safe, settled and really enjoy being there.
The school is lovely and welcoming. Everyone’s friendly and you can tell the staff genuinely care – it’s a really positive place to be.
Wellington has a real community feel. It feels like everyone’s working together to support the children and families.

English
Intent
Reading and writing lies at the heart of all great learning. We believe that every child has the right to leave primary school with a good acquisition of the English language, having developed the key skills of reading and writing needed to function in the wider world.
Through a use of varied and rich texts, we develop a passion for reading and stimulating opportunities for writing. Children will be introduced to a range of authors, forms, styles and text types, in order to broaden their skills and ignite their interests within the world of English. By linking our texts to our topic-based curriculum, we also intend to develop the children’s awareness of how English is interlinked with the wider curriculum.
Our reading and writing curriculum is thoroughly planned and consistently monitored and adapted to ensure that children are provided with the best opportunities to develop the following key skills:
Reading
read with fluency, expression and intonation
Writing
Phonics
Across the Federation, we follow the 'Read Write Inc.' phonics programme, which is one of the validated systematic synthetic phonics (SSP) teaching programmes. For more information, please click the link below to visit the dedicated phonics & early reading page.

Maths
Intent
Our aim is to deliver a high-quality mathematics education provides a foundation for understanding the world, the ability to reason and problem solve mathematically and a sense of enjoyment and curiosity about the subject. Our approach to maths is linked to the HIAS model, based on a cyclical curriculum which enables the children make links across the domains and build on previous learning on each unit so the learning is embedded. With an aim to continually improve and develop our curriculum, we also collaborate with the Maths Hub.
All pupils are encouraged by the belief that by working hard at maths they can succeed.
Pupils are taught through whole-class interactive teaching, where the focus is on all pupils working together on the same lesson content at the same time endeavouring to following a Maths Mastery approach; this ensures that all can master concepts before moving to the next part of the curriculum sequence, allowing no pupil to be left behind.
If a pupil fails to grasp a concept or procedure, this is identified quickly and early intervention ensures the pupil is ready to move forward with the whole class in the next lesson.
Pupils who grasp concepts rapidly are challenged through being offered rich and sophisticated problems before any acceleration through new content.
Lesson design identifies the new mathematics that is to be taught, the key points, the difficult points and a carefully sequenced journey through the learning.

Science
Intent
Science across Bold Futures aims to provide children the opportunity to investigate their wide world, ensuring that they are building a curiosity about the subject and giving them the confidence to ask 'why'. We support children to develop a core foundation of scientific knowledge which will enable them to have the confidence and correct language to form predictions, plan investigations and explain and critically analyse their findings showing an understating of cause and effect.
After ensuring children have a basic understanding of necessary scientific concepts, we use a problem solving approach and, where appropriate, teachers put investigations into a relevant context - whether that may be linked to their topic or the children’s lives.
Our aim as a school is to create children who are independently able to plan and carry out fair and well-designed investigations to test given problems with a critical eye and support them to assess their own and others’ results. This is achieved via teacher modelling, guided experiments and group work; giving the child a sense of independence and ownership of their learning.

MFL (Spanish)
Intent
Key Stage 2 children at Wellington will be inquisitive and have a deeper understanding of the world, having expanded their knowledge of other cultures through the language of Spanish speaking countries. They will be able to communicate practically in Spanish and be ready and curious for other language opportunities in Secondary School.
All Key Stage 2, Wellington pupils will have had opportunities to regularly hear and speak Spanish, through the teaching of key vocabulary and the provision of contextualised events and experiences in which children can communicate for practical purposes.

Relationships Education (and RSE)
We are dedicated to keeping your child safe. This extends beyond the classroom and beyond their time with us. To this end, we are always looking for ways to improve and update our curriculum to ensure that it reflects the needs of our community.
We hold a 'Healthy Relationships Week' each year across both schools. Lessons are taught by class teachers, alongside the class LSAs. 1:1 adult support will also be maintained if your child receives this.
Our curriculum is developed by our Deputy Head/PSHE Lead, to ensure that all content is sensitive, culturally-reflective and developmentally-appropriate.
The week focuses on how children can have safe and healthy relationships, how they can keep themselves safe online as well as in person, what happens during puberty, the biological differences between males and females and, in year 6 only, the scientific facts of conception. This is part of our PSHE curriculum which supports our child's holistic health: their social, emotional, physical, mental and personal health.
Parents and carers have the opportunity to view and respond to the curriculum content in two ways. We hold a consultation before teachers are trained in the curriculum. This allows us to take into account your opinion on the learning and make any adaptations that we deem necessary. In addition, we will make the planning available on this page and alert parents/carers to our online survey.
After the sessions are held, we also hold a child survey at school as this allows us to make adaptations to our curriculum ready for the following year.
All children take part in the sessions as these are statutory. Please see our Healthy Relationships policy (via the link below) for more information on the right to remove from the Sex Education lesson.

Music
Intent
Children will develop a rich appreciation and deep love for a variety of musical forms. We will engage and inspire all children through a wide range of experiences so that they have increased self-confidence and creativity.
Children will listen to, appreciate and discuss a wide range of high-quality live and recorded music drawn from different traditions, cultures and times, and from great composers and musicians. Children will sing and play musically with increasing control, accuracy, fluency and expression, performing in solo and ensemble contexts, feeling a sense of pride and achievement in themselves. Children will develop an understanding of musical composition, by organising and manipulating ideas within musical structures and reproducing sounds from aural memory. They will compose, record and perform music for a range of purposes using the dimensions of music, using and understanding staff and other musical notations.
